lessons.keep: Give each presenter one distinct job and one supporting artifact.
lessons.avoid: Avoid using rising revenue overlays as proof of typical customer income.
lessons.open: Presenter identities are taken from on-screen labels; earnings, offer eligibility, product execution, full-rate transitions and audio remain unverified.
try: Show a Tin customer explaining one campaign problem, then cut directly to its brief, approval and published output.
Use a branded visual metaphor only after a complete product action, keeping the CTA and any offer terms readable.

comparison.story: Frame conventional work as frustration. → State an alternative and hand off. → Connect expertise with a sellable community. → Present business revenue and wallet features. → Connect digital earnings to spending. → Explain product scope in a virtual showroom. → Expand distribution and motivation. → Reduce the expertise barrier with a testimonial-style appeal. → Present launch incentive and distribution. → Create a memorable money metaphor. → Finish with a comic afterthought.
